summary: Skamania County summit with a 1934 L-4 lookout cab later replaced and removed; staffed into the early 1960s; a foundation remains and hikers reach the summit by trail.

facts.design: L-4 cab built 1934, later an R-6 flat cab (register and firelookout.com); a rustic flat-roofed house, 15 ft 4 in square, was built in 1954 per a newspaper item
facts.status_note: Cab removed; a hiking guide reports that the remains of a foundation are on the summit

access.note: Summit reached by hiking trails on Gifford Pinchot National Forest land; the north approach needs high clearance and AWD

visit.trail_note: A trail from the parking lot merges with the abandoned lookout road after several switchbacks

events.note: A newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts describes the lookout at Silver Star reporting on the Dole fire; the sources do not describe the structure then
L-4 cab built in 1934 (register and firelookout.com)
Aircraft Warning Service station, activated March 11, 1942; AWS funds paid for sleeping quarters and a woodshed
AWS station deactivated October 15, 1943; the Forest Service kept the site as a fire detection point
Anne Donnelly had kept the lookout for five years, per an October 2, 1952 Longview Daily News item
Wikipedia dates installation of a lookout on the higher north peak to 1952; this conflicts with the 1934 cab and the 1952 staffing item
New 15 ft 4 in flat-roofed house built July and August 1954, per a September 1954 Longview Daily News item
Register gives R-6 flat cab replacing the L-4 in 1955
Mrs. Robert B. Donnelly said to have served as lookout for several years (Longview Daily News, July 11, 1959)
Vernon Kinney was lookout for the summer; last staffing in the sources read
Wikipedia says the north-peak lookout was removed by 1969; the register says the R-6 cab was later removed, with no date
Registered July 17, 2012 on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register

notes_for_editor: Dates disagree. The first lookout is unclear: a 1929 item mentions a lookout at Silver Star, the register and firelookout.com give a 1934 L-4 cab, and Wikipedia dates a north-peak lookout to 1952; the 1952 staffing item suggests a lookout existed before 1952. Replacement is 1954 (newspaper, July-August construction) versus 1955 (register); both are kept. Wikipedia's 1952 and 1969 dates are leads, and its cited source was not checked. The brief's height_m 4.3 is unsourced in our reads and was left out of facts. The brief's access 'unknown' became public because sources call the summit a popular hiking destination; no formal access policy was read, so review that level. Possible photo lead, not read or licence-checked: a 1958 aerial view of Silver Star Mountain Lookout, Gifford Pinchot NF, on the Internet Archive (usdafs-32747039864). Research used 1 WebSearch and 8 page reads (one listing page not used), over the per-tower budget, to check the Wikipedia conflict.
